title: Remote work and home-office policy
text: Employees who work remotely for two or more days each week may request a monthly home-office allowance. The allowance covers ordinary utility and internet costs; it is not a reimbursement for furniture or computer hardware. Submit the request in Workday before the tenth day of the month. A manager must approve the arrangement before Finance releases the allowance. Remote workers must use the company VPN for internal systems and must not print confidential material at a shared workspace.

title: Equipment procurement and approval
text: Use the equipment request form to buy a laptop, monitor, headset, or other employee hardware. The employee's manager approves requests up to 2,000 EUR. The IT operations lead reviews the technical specification, and Finance approves any request above that amount. Choose a standard laptop whenever one meets the role's needs. Purchases made personally without an approved request cannot be expensed as company equipment.

title: Information-security baseline
text: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for email, source control, and the virtual private network (VPN). Use the approved authenticator application; SMS is permitted only as a temporary recovery method. Report a suspected phishing message through the mail client. Do not share a VPN account, an MFA code, or a password with a colleague or support agent.

title: Expense Policy 2025
text: Employees may claim necessary business travel, customer meals, and approved software subscriptions. Attach an itemised receipt and submit the claim within 30 days. A manager approves ordinary claims; Finance reviews claims above 1,000 EUR. Home internet is covered only by the separate remote-work allowance. Personal equipment and ordinary commuting costs are not reimbursable expenses.

title: Home-office allowance guide
text: The home-office allowance is a fixed monthly payment for eligible remote employees. It contributes to broadband and utility costs without requiring a monthly receipt. It does not pay for a desk, chair, monitor, or a personal mobile telephone. New participants need manager approval and must update their work-location record before the allowance begins.

title: Aurora release readiness checklist
text: Before the Aurora customer portal goes live, the release manager confirms the production migration, rollback plan, monitoring dashboard, on-call rotation, and customer communication. Product signs off on the acceptance criteria and Engineering signs off on capacity testing. The release is ready only after a staging rehearsal succeeds and the incident channel has an assigned commander. Record the go-live decision in the release ticket.

title: Aurora incident review: 2025-02-14
text: The Aurora portal was unavailable for 23 minutes after a deployment introduced an invalid cache key. Requests bypassed the cache and exhausted the API worker pool. The on-call engineer rolled back the release, restored normal traffic, and opened a follow-up task for a pre-deployment cache validation. The incident did not expose customer data. The next release must include a canary check for cache-key compatibility and an alert for worker-pool saturation.

title: Meridian quarterly budget review
text: The Meridian programme has 84,000 EUR remaining for the second half of the year. The proposed spend covers a data-quality contractor, two customer research sessions, and the Nimbus Analytics renewal. Finance asked the team to obtain a renewal quote before committing the final amount. No Aurora release or incident costs are included in this forecast.

title: Object-storage recovery runbook
text: For accidental deletion from object storage, first stop lifecycle jobs and identify the affected bucket and version IDs. Restore the required object versions from the retention window, then verify checksums and application access before reopening writes. Escalate if the retention window has expired. Backups are for recovery; they do not change the legal retention schedule for customer records.

title: Public API rate limits
text: The public API returns HTTP 429 when a client exceeds its request quota. Use the Retry-After response header and exponential backoff. Do not retry a failed write blindly; first determine whether the original request completed. Partners that need a higher quota should contact developer support with their expected traffic profile.

title: Parental leave
text: Employees who become a parent through birth, adoption, or foster placement may take 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Notify People Operations at least eight weeks before the expected start when practical. Managers should agree on a coverage plan and treat adoption and birth requests under the same leave entitlement.

title: Customer data retention notice
text: We retain customer account information for seven years after account closure when it is needed for tax, contractual, or legal obligations. We delete or anonymise data that is no longer needed under the retention schedule. Backup copies follow a separate rolling recovery window and are not used to extend the legal retention period.

title: Nimbus Analytics renewal quote needed by Friday
text: The Nimbus Analytics subscription expires on 31 March. Send the number of seats and the proposed annual budget so Procurement can request the renewal quote. Finance approval is required before accepting the contract.

title: Security awareness course due 20 March
text: The annual security-awareness course must be completed by 20 March. The course covers phishing reports, password safety, and multi-factor authentication. Employees who use the VPN must complete it before their next access review.

title: Q1 customer feedback summary
text: Customers value the Aurora portal's search and export features, but several reported that the analytics dashboard takes too long to load. The most common request was a faster dashboard after selecting a large date range. The product team will measure dashboard response time and show progress for long-running exports. This report is about user experience, not API quota errors.

title: Travel expense audit findings
text: Conference hotel stays, rail tickets, and airport transfers were reimbursed when the traveller attached itemised receipts and an approved trip record. Several late hotel claims required additional manager review because they were submitted after the 30-day expense deadline. The audit found no evidence that home-office broadband payments were charged as travel expenses.
